mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 0.5% coincident with a rise in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening consumer demand offset by a nascent housing recovery, resulting in flat to slightly positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -0.5% AND HOUST > previous 3-month average
regime_hint: late-cycle demand softening with housing stabilization
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative or the Rank IC for the signal is below 0.05 over any 3-year period.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) falling below 5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as profit margins compress.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when UNRATE < 5% for three consecutive months (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both CPIAUCSL (above 3% YoY) and FEDFUNDS (above 4%) for two consecutive months signals a dual shock of inflation and aggressive policy tightening, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 3% YoY AND FEDFUNDS > 4% for two consecutive months
regime_hint: high inflation and restrictive policy regime
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when both CPIAUCSL > 3% and FEDFUNDS > 4% for two consecutive months (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 1% signals weakening consumer demand, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as market participants anticipate lower corporate revenues.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS falls by more than 1% in a month (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE in the same month signals a labor market expansion with slack reduction, which historically coincides with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to improved corporate earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and UNRATE both increase month-over-month
regime_hint: loose labor market transitioning to tight
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during months when both PAYEMS and UNRATE increase (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of at least 0.3% for four consecutive months signals a manufacturing slowdown, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to expected earnings downgrades.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.3% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained INDPRO declines below -0.3% for four consecutive months (t-test p > 0.10).
